correctness.rationale: The parameter reduction to r=min/max is exact by common scaling and swapping lambda,mu together with x,y. The embedding T(s,t)=(s,t,s-t) converts the hexagonal norm to the sup norm on a two-dimensional subspace. For equal output coordinates the quotient is at most 1. For distinct output coordinates, weighted AM-GM and the exact dual-norm lemma reduce the global optimization to minimizing a one-variable function in z=kappa^2. Its stationary point is feasible exactly when r^4+r^2<=1; otherwise the minimum lies on z=1/r. The two explicit families attain the respective upper bounds, including the transition point.
risks: The proof depends on the exact dual norm of coordinate functionals on the affine-regular hexagon; the bundled checker enumerates all six vertices and all distinct coordinate-pair sign patterns.
The deterministic numerical search is supplementary only and is not used to establish the continuum supremum.

value.rationale: The result determines the entire two-parameter invariant up to its intrinsic ratio symmetry, rather than a single test value. The affine-regular hexagon is the canonical nonsmooth Radon plane and a standard benchmark for planar Banach geometry. The exact golden-ratio threshold marks a genuine change in the optimizing dual certificate and extremizer geometry. The proof method—three-coordinate embedding plus optimized dual support—can be reused for weighted geometric constants on other polyhedral norms.
risks: The contribution is an exact canonical-space profile, not a classification of all polygonal Banach planes.
